newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Rule changes aid Hungary forint trading - official.
newsitem.headline: Rule changes aid Hungary forint trading - official.

text.p: Regulatory changes in Hungary's interbank foreign currency market will enable market players to follow the movements of the forint more easily, the National Bank of Hungary (NBH) said on Wednesday.
The NBH on January 1 replaced the Ecu in the currency basket, against which the forint floats, by the mark. The basket now made up of 30 percent dollar and 70 percent mark.

It also changed the basis for the forint fix from the mid-rate of the forint against the currency basket to the average of the 11 o'clock dollar/forint quote of the ten most active banks on the interbank foreign currency market.

An NBH official, who asked not to be named, told Reuters the Ecu market is less liquid than that of the mark, and that sometimes caused difficulties for market players seeking to hedge their positions.
"They will get a price for the dollar/mark sooner and more easily, even for smaller amounts," he said. "The exchange rates also better reflect the real picture of the market (from January 1).
The change of the basis for the official daily forint fixing also served that purpose, he said.
"We are trying to follow the market in that respect, too," the official said. @

The previous fixing method, based on the mid-rate in the central bank's 4.5 percent wide intervention range, did not reflect the real market value of the forint, which usually trades close to the NBH resistance level (bid) and not the midrate, the official said.
"It was already unrealistic that we used the midrate, while the forint moved was almost always near the resistance level (bid) in the past two years," he said. @

The change in the fixing method is a substantial technical assistance to those who are obliged by the law to account for their transactions on the basis of daily forint fixings, the official and Hungarian interbank dealers said.
